subject.title: Track OpenClaw seams needed for full imported-plugin parity

question: Should OpenClaw expose any of the requested imported-plugin parity seams as stable public SDK contracts, and if so which narrowly scoped capability should be designed first?
rationale: The request introduces new host API and security-boundary surface rather than repairing an established contract; source-level implementation cannot safely choose the permanent public API shape.

options.title: Start with a narrow approval/connector RFC
options.body: Define lifecycle, authorization, authentication, and compatibility constraints for one security-sensitive seam before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Accept only non-security bundle projections first
options.body: Scope an initial contract to validated bundle settings or LSP defaults while deferring approvals and connectors for separate security review.

options.title: Keep parity intentionally partial
options.body: Document the unsupported mappings and retain the existing host boundary until a broader OpenClaw SDK direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Start with a narrow approval/connector RFC
recommendation.body: Define lifecycle, authorization, authentication, and compatibility constraints for one security-sensitive seam before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: The member-authored issue is the only concrete routing signal available in the supplied context; code-history ownership could not be verified.
